title: Russia Turns to Expensive Asian Gasoline Imports as Second Fuel Crisis Wave Hits
detail: Russia's domestic fuel crisis enters a second wave as Moscow is forced to purchase expensive gasoline imports from Asian markets to offset ongoing refinery shortfalls. The costly import strategy signals continued stress on domestic refining capacity, with major facilities at Omsk and Saratov struggling to meet national demand.

title: Petrol available at just 28% of Russian stations as Moscow queues return
detail: Nationwide petrol availability fell to 28% of filling stations on Aug 20, down from 41% a week earlier, according to the monitoring app Gdebenz — with damaged refineries now accounting for 54% of national refining capacity. Yandex Fuel showed AI-92 available at just 1 in 10 stations in Moscow, where queues formed at pumps for the first time in this wave; Gazprom Neft capped purchases at 40 liters per fill-up and Tatneft at 50 liters of petrol / 60 liters of diesel. Separately, Meduza reported strict fuel-sale limits now cover at least 59 Russian regions, with another 17 seeing localized disruption, and a related motor-oil shortage emerging from a lack of imported additives.
